title: A negative-curvature normal barrier on an algebraic cone that is not a hyperbolicity cone
author: Alec Kriebel
description: An explicit negative-curvature normal barrier on a known one-sided power cone, together with an obstruction to every defining hyperbolic polynomial in three variables.
abstract_source: Complete original one-paragraph abstract from deposited main.tex; matched to published PDF p1. TeX preserved verbatim in abstract-source.tex. Unicode/plain-text notation changes only; no claim or qualification omitted.
abstract_original_tex:
We give an explicit affirmative answer to Tun\c{c}el's 2017 existential
question about algebraic convex cones with negative-curvature normal
barriers. The one-sided power cone
$K=\{(x,y,z)\geq0:xy^2\geq z^3\}$ admits the barrier
$F=-25\log\bigl(z(xy^2-z^3)\bigr)$ with parameter $100$ and
$D^3F(a)[h,u,u]\leq0$ for every $a\in\inter K$, $h\in K$, and
$u\in\R^3$. Exact polynomial and positive-semidefinite certificates prove
the curvature inequality, including its degenerate directions. A boundary
divisibility argument rules out every homogeneous hyperbolic polynomial
defining $K$ in $\R^3$. The cone itself is a known member of Hildebrand's
classification; the contribution here is the explicit barrier certificate
and its verification for the stated existential problem.
abstract: We give an explicit affirmative answer to Tunçel’s 2017 existential question about algebraic convex cones with negative-curvature normal barriers. The one-sided power cone K = {(x,y,z) ≥ 0: xy² ≥ z³} admits the barrier F = −25 log(z(xy² − z³)) with parameter 100 and D³F(a)[h,u,u] ≤ 0 for every a ∈ int K, h ∈ K, and u ∈ ℝ³. Exact polynomial and positive-semidefinite certificates prove the curvature inequality, including its degenerate directions. A boundary divisibility argument rules out every homogeneous hyperbolic polynomial defining K in ℝ³. The cone itself is a known member of Hildebrand’s classification; the contribution here is the explicit barrier certificate and its verification for the stated existential problem.

plain_language: Barrier functions help optimization algorithms stay inside a feasible region by growing without bound near its boundary. This note studies an additional derivative-sign condition called negative curvature. Here that term describes the barrier’s third derivatives, rather than the curvature of physical space.

The example is the known cone of nonnegative triples satisfying xy² ≥ z³. The paper presents a specific logarithmic barrier and proves the required sign condition for every interior point, every direction in the closed cone and every real test vector.

The same cone cannot be the hyperbolicity cone of any homogeneous polynomial in its original three-dimensional space. These two properties supply the kind of example requested in Tunçel’s 2017 existential question.

The cone and earlier self-concordant barriers were already known. The note’s stated contribution is the explicit additional negative-curvature certificate and its accompanying nonhyperbolicity argument. It makes no first-ever priority claim.
result: For K = {(x,y,z) ∈ ℝ³: x,y,z ≥ 0, xy² ≥ z³}, Theorem 1 states that K is a regular algebraic convex cone and F = −25 log(z(xy²−z³)) is a parameter-100 normal barrier on int K.
The asserted curvature inequality is D³F(a)[h,u,u] ≤ 0 for every a ∈ int K, h ∈ K and u ∈ ℝ³, including zero and boundary cone directions.
No homogeneous polynomial of any degree in three variables has K as its hyperbolicity cone. The result concerns the original ambient space.
why_it_works: Concavity of the weighted geometric mean x^(1/3)y^(2/3) gives convexity of K. A Hessian decomposition and a mixed third-derivative bound establish self-concordance after scaling; logarithmic homogeneity gives parameter 100.

Diagonal automorphisms reduce each interior base point to (r,1,1), with r>1. Every cone direction is a nonnegative combination of (t³,1,t), t≥0, and the x-axis direction. Exact minor and square identities certify the derivative matrix; a separate block and Gram certificate cover the degenerate directions.

Any defining hyperbolic polynomial would vanish along the cone’s curved boundary and hence contain xy²−z³ as a factor. Along a suitable line, this factor has a nonreal root pair for every possible interior hyperbolicity direction, giving a contradiction.
limitations: The theorem is for this one-sided nonnegative power cone. It does not claim a result for the sign-symmetric power cone, arbitrary exponents or all regular cones.
The base point must lie in int K. The cone direction may lie anywhere in the closed cone; the inequality is semidefinite and is degenerate for some directions.

Parameter100 is an explicit sufficient value and is deliberately nonoptimal. Roy–Xiao already give a parameter 3 self-concordant barrier on the same cone; no self-concordance-parameter improvement is claimed.
The nonhyperbolicity conclusion excludes defining homogeneous polynomials in the original three-dimensional space. It does not exclude projections or higher-dimensional lifts.

The universal inequalities rest on the analytic argument and exact symbolic identities. The deposited finite rational checks are supplementary evidence. This scope review read the two submitted checkers but did not execute them.

Historical priority, full novelty and worldwide current-open status remain unverified. This bounded primary-source review does not exclude every inaccessible or unindexed predecessor; the 2026 Hildebrand journal text and related OpenReview prepublication remain full-text coverage gaps.

This preprint was prepared with extensive AI assistance and is unrefereed. AI-assisted checks and accompanying AI reviews are neither external human peer review nor formal proof-assistant certification.

background.title: Levent Tunçel, Polynomial optimization with a focus on hyperbolic polynomials (OWR14/2017)
background.note: Open Problem 1 on printed p. 799 asks for the existential algebraic-cone example. This historical wording does not certify present-day openness.

background.title: Yu. Nesterov and Levent Tunçel, Local Superlinear Convergence of Polynomial-Time Interior-Point Methods for Hyperbolic Cone Optimization Problems
background.note: Provides normal-barrier and negative-curvature conventions and established closure/background results.

background.title: Joachim Dahl, Levent Tunçel and Lieven Vandenberghe, New complexity bounds for primal–dual interior-point algorithms in conic optimization
background.note: Definitions §§2.2 and3.1 match the stated derivative properties; §6 asks the broader universal cone question. The v2 record, PDF and HTML have separately recorded dates.

background.title: Roland Hildebrand, Analytic formulas for complete hyperbolic affine spheres
background.note: Theorem 3.2 family 5 already contains the underlying cone after the specified coordinate permutation and exponent specialization.

background.title: Scott Roy and Lin Xiao, On self-concordant barriers for generalized power cones (2018)
background.note: Theorem 2 supplies a parameter 3 self-concordant barrier on the same nonnegative power cone. This is prior barrier credit; the cited theorem does not assert the additional cone-direction negative-curvature sign.
